video_title: Eastern Conference Finals Preview - Knicks Heavy Favorites?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' rest advantage and O.G. Anunoby's health for playoffs
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks have nine or ten days off between games. That is a really good thing for O.G. Anunoby.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Knicks have had nine days, I think? Nine or ten days off between games. That is a really good thing for O.G. Anunoby. Hopefully he'll be back from that hamstring issue.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Pelton
text_blocks.text: I guess it'll be on the ninth day. It's Tuesday. They last played Sunday. Yeah, by all it seems he'll be ready to go for Game 1.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: So, you have one team that's well-rested and one team that's coming off back-to-back seven-game series. The Cavs will have some rhythm.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' impressive offense against Cavs' weakest defense
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs defense is going to be stressed against that New York offense.
quotes.quote: The Knicks offensive production has been dramatically impressive. I would argue that of the eight teams left in the second round, do I want to say this? Do I want to say this? Do the Cavs have the weakest defense? They certainly have the weakest defense of the remaining teams. The Cavs defense is going to be stressed against that New York offense.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Pelton
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavs' disappointing playoff run despite talent
quotes.excerpt: This has been a very disappointing showing through the first two rounds despite them being in the Conference Finals.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Pelton
text_blocks.text: The Cavs have been pretty awful through these first two rounds of the playoffs. I mean, Brian will tell, I mean Brian's the leader of Cavs Corner, will you not say this has been a very disappointing showing through the first two rounds despite them being in the Conference Finals? That they played lower than what your expectations would be for the amount of talent they have?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I think the point out is they're eight and six so far in the playoffs. If a team is eight and six, they very clearly have exploitable flaws and also their flaws that, you know, undercut them.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Pelton
text_blocks.text: Now that being said, they are, these are the two teams that at the start of the year were expected to be here. That is the irony of the situation. The Cavs and the Knicks entered the season as the co-favorites in the East for a reason. They both have a lot of talent. You saw in this Game 7 today, the Cavs played much like the team they were supposed to be. That is why this has been sort of an infuriating run for them because they have not really looked like that team for the most of most of these playoffs. They have weezed their way through a Raptors series where the Raptors were all banged up with injuries and couldn't really score. And they then weezed their way through the series against the Pistons who had one guy who could really handle the ball and often couldn't really score and still almost won the series anyway.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Tactical adjustments and Ausar Thompson's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: The tactical adjustment we made was avoiding Ausar Thompson. We were just like if he's near the ball, throw it to somebody else.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Hey McMahon, fresh quote from Kenny Atkinson. The tactical adjustment we made was avoiding Ausar Thompson. We were just like if he's near the ball, throw it to somebody else. Bontemps is like, put him on the bench. He's not a starter.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: But listen, and yes, avoid him. It was avoid him on one end and invite him to shoot it on the other.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Pelton
text_blocks.text: Yeah, it's fine. It's true. I mean, they should have, I mean, they would have been better off benching him honestly and playing him off the bench instead. But anyway, that's a separate discussion.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: You know, Tony Allen, one of the all-time great perimeter defenders, he basically said, they're getting guys who have jumpers like me out of the league now. And Ausar Thompson is a modern-day, you know,

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Pelton
text_blocks.text: He's a bigger, stronger, faster Tony Allen, that's what he is.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: That's what he is. And we'll see if he can develop a jumper.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I remember when I covered the series Memphis against Oklahoma City. And Tony Allen, this is Durant like pretty much when he was just ascending into being. Tony Allen had hounded Durant so much that there would be times where Durant would come off, he would run around screens and Durant would catch the ball. Allen would be ten feet behind him, eight feet behind him. And Durant would immediately turn his body and protect the ball because Allen had been there so much that he just assumed he would. His defense was so strong that he didn't even have to be there to defend him. And so, when you compare somebody to Tony Allen, it is a defensively, it is a very high compliment.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Pelton
text_blocks.text: I voted Ausar Thompson first-team All-Defense. He's a tremendous defensive player.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Offensively he's got a lot of room for growth.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Pelton
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavs' defensive challenge against Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: The guy who's probably best suited to guard Jalen Brunson on the Cavs is Keon Ellis, who's barely played.
quotes.quote: Donovan Mitchell and James Harden have looked tired at times during this series and during this run. They've had to play every other day for a month, as you said, they've had to play two seven-game series. The Knicks are very rested. The Knicks have a lot of guys they can throw at both of those guys. The Cavs, ironically, the guy who's probably best suited to guard Jalen Brunson on the Cavs is Keon Ellis, who's barely played. Other than that, they don't really have a lot of guys to throw at Jalen Brunson.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' shooting negating Cavs' interior defense
quotes.excerpt: The strength of the Cavs defense is obviously their two big guys, is Mobley and Allen.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Well, and the strength of the Cavs defense is obviously their two big guys, is Mobley and Allen. And against the Pistons, Mobley and Allen could pack the paint and basically just put a wall around the rim. And you cannot do that especially against the Knicks starting lineup where they've got the self-proclaimed greatest shooting big man of all time. And, you know, they can they can put five guys out there that, you know, even Josh Hart, you have to respect him as a three-point threat.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Pelton
text_blocks.text: I mean, he shot 39% from three this year. That's been one of the huge revelations of the season.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: And you have to fear as a three-point threat. You know, if Anunoby's healthy, you have to fear him as a three-point threat. They can, so they can spread the floor where that that's the biggest weakness of the Pistons is just that you can really clog things up for them on the defensive end.
